Committee on private universities
*101. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of private universities
established under various State legislations
and whether they have acquired the status
of research universities;
(b) whether Government have received
any suggestion from the University Grants
Commission for constituting a high level
committee to look into the fee and course
structure of private universities; and
(c) whether Government intend to set
up some new central universities, including
some world class campuses, and if so, the
number of such universities?
Ongoing power projects
*102. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of ongoing power projects
in the country and the progress made, so
far, State-wise;
(b) the amount spent on those projects
during the last three years, State-wise;
and
(c) by when those projects are likely to
be completed?
Private investment in education
*103. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal from
any source, including the Planning
Commission, to set up a policy frame-work
for facilitating private investment in
education;
(b) if so, the details and the present
status thereof;
(c) whether there is any proposal/plan
to tap sources of finance, other than the
Central Government and State Government
funds, to set up new institutions and to
expand the existing institutions in education,
especially higher education;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the number of universities, Central
Universities, deemed institutions as on
date, State-wise and category-wise?

34
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Uniform education system
†*104. SHRI SHATRUGHAN
SINHA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government agree with
Bihar Government's scheme to implement
a uniform education system;
(b) if so, whether Government intend
to provide necessary funds to the State
Government for implementing the said
scheme;
(c) whether any proposal has been
received from the State Government in this
regard; and
(d) if so, Government's policy in this
regard?
De-limitation of constituencies
*105. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the De-limitation
Commission has completed the task of
delimiting Assembly and Parliamentary
constituencies in the country;
(b) if not, the States in which the de-
limitation has been completed;
(c) the States where the de-limitation
process is continuing at various stages;
(d) by which date the Commission is
expected to submit its report;
(e) whether Government are rethinking
on de-limitation and whether the process
is likely to be started de novo;
(f) whether population criteria adopted
by the Commission has been found to be
counterproductive and undesirable; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Share of Punjab in education cess
*106. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the Central assistance, out of the
educational cess, given to Punjab during
2005-06, 2006-07 and that earmarked for
2007-08, for various educational schemes,
scheme-wise and year-wise; and
(b) whether the state was given its share
so as to fully utilize the central assistance,
if so, the details thereof and if not, the
reasons therefor?
Fast Track Courts for pending cases
*107. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of cases pending in
the courts in the country, State-wise;
(b) whether Government propose to
start new Fast Track Courts for the
clearance of pending cases; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Hiring of women and infants for
begging
*108. DR. P.C. ALEXANDER: Will the
Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a massive
increase in the practice of hiring the services
of women and infants by beggar mafia for
begging at public places in big cities of the
country, particularly in Delhi; and

35
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to prevent the exploitation of
women and children by the beggar mafia?
Development policy for linguistic
minorities
*109. DR. E.M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN: Will the Minister of
MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are formulating
linguistic minorities and their development
policy;
(b) if so, the salient features thereof,
State-wise and Union Territory-wise; and
(c) the protection and development
policies formulated for Tamil minorities in
Delhi and other northern States?
Metering of feeders, distribution
transformers and consumer
connections
*110. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Accelerated Power
Development and Reform Programme
(APDRP) envisaged 100 per cent metering
of feeders, distribution transformers (DTs)
and consumer connections;
(b) if so, the details of the progress made
thereon; and
(c) the measures taken to complete 100
per cent feeder, DT and consumer metering
in all the ongoing and completed APDRP
projects, within a clearly defined time-
frame?
Power generation cost of NTPC
†*111. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that cost of power
generation by the National Thermal Power
Corporation is higher than that of other
private sector companies;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the bids
of private sector companies for Sasan Ultra
Mega Power Project was lower, as
compared to the bid of the National
Thermal Power Corporation; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction in that
regard?
Pending cases in courts
†*112. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL: Will the Minister of LAW
AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
cases are pending for long in district courts,
High Courts and the Supreme Court;
(b) if so, the time-limit for disposal of
cases in the Supreme Court, High Courts,
district courts and subordinate courts;
(c) whether Government would
consider disposing off single point cases
pending for long on single point basis; and
(d) if so, what provisions would be made
therefor in the enactments?

36
Women education centres in the
North Eastern Region
*113. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of women education
centres set up by the Central Government
for illiterate women, in the North Eastern
Region (NER), particularly in Sikkim,
during the last three years;
(b) the number of women benefited
therefrom during that period, year-wise
and State-wise; and
(c) the details of amount allocated and
spent by each centre in NER, State-wise?
UNESCO's references on education
in India
*114. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
ascertained the references about education
in the country in a recent publication by
the International Institute of Educational
Planning, an associate body of UNESCO;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether Government agree with
such references;
(e) if not, whether Government have
raised the issue with the concerned
authorities in UNESCO; and
(f) if so, the remedial steps being taken
in this regard?
IIT in Kerala
*115. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Kerala Government has
forwarded a proposal for setting up of an
IIT in that State;
(b) if so, whether the location for the
proposed IIT has been identified;
(c) whether the competent officials of
the Ministry have visited the proposed site;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the approval for the
proposal has been granted; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Funds for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
*116. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government intend to
sanction more funds under the Sarva
Shiksha Abhiyan during the Eleventh Five
Year Plan; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of food parks
†*117. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up thirty food parks in the country, for
providing better prices to farmers for their
produce, under food processing industries;
(b) if so, the places where these food
parks would be set up; and

horticulture produces and floriculture and

farming in backward regions like Vidarbha

Auction of coal blocks
*118. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in sharp
contrast to the Coal Ministry's views to
auction coal blocks to various sectors his
Ministry has strongly opposed the move;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether his Ministry has written to
PMO in this regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Approval for private educational
institutions
*119. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that promoters
of private educational institutions like
medical, dental and engineering colleges,
require approval from the Central
Government;
(b) if so, the reasons why the promoters
of private colleges/institutions providing
MBA and BBA courses are not taking
similar approval from the All India Council
of Technical Education (AICTE) and the
University Grants Commission (UGC); and
(c) the steps Government propose to
take against such institutions, including the
Indian Institute of Planning and
Management, New Delhi, to safeguard the
interst of student community?
Sale price of natural gas
*120. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the sale price of natural gas from D6 block
of KG basin is being increased abnormally,
which would adversely affect the power
sector;
(b) whether he has taken up the matter
with his counterpart in the Ministry of
Petroleum and Natural Gas and suggested
some guidelines, based on which the sale
price of natural gas is to be approved by
them;
(c) if so, the details of guidelines and
the reaction of the Ministry of Petroleum
and Natural Gas thereto; and
(d) the action being contemplated to
ensure that approved sale price is in line
with the present benchmarked price, signed
between NTPC and RIL?

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;

Total number of questions — 155
173
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Research studies on global warming
744. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRA-
IAH: Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether the research institutes under
the Ministry are working in a coordinated
manner to resolve issues pertaining to global
warming, that are either directly or
indirectly affecting the socio-economic
growth of the country;
(b) if so, whether research studies are
done on melting down of Himalayan
Glaciers, increased occurrence of cyclones,
particularly in Andhra Pradesh, flash floods,
cloud bursts, etc.;
(c) if so, the details thereof, alongwith
the breakthroughs made, if any; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Setting up of food parks in
Uttarakhand
†745. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal for
setting up of food parks in Uttarakhand
during 2007-08;
(b) if so, whether the locations have
been earmarked for this purpose;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the steps Government
propose to do away with the delays in this
regard?
Monitoring on meat and meat
products
746. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal before
Government for overseeing or monitoring
the meat and meat products;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is also a proposal to
set up the National Meat Board;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the Board would oversee
the growth and promote meat and poultry
sector in the country; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?

174
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Indo-France joint panel for food
processing sector
†747. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether an Indo-France joint panel
has been formed for the cooperation in the
food processing sector;
(b) if so, whether the technology for
agro products to be included under the food
processing, would also be transferred; and
(c) the food stuffs which would be
covered under the food processing sector
between India and France?
Public sector food processing industry
for Nagpur
748. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Nagpur is
the biggest producer of good quality
oranges and has great potential for food
processing industry;
(b) if so, whether any food processing
industry has been set up there in the public
sector;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Capacity of food processing and cold
storages
749. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any scheme to enhance the
capacity of food processing and cold
storages in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total extent of loss suffered due
to poor storage facilities during the last three
years;
(d) the total amount allocated to
improve the storage facilities during that
period, State-wise; and
(e) the extent of increase registered in
the capacity of cold storages by each State?
Fee hike in higher education
750. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal from
any source, including the Planning
Commission during 2007, to increase fees
to meet at least 20 per cent of recurring
cost on higher education;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
present status of the above proposal;
(c) the details of ratio of existing fees
and recurring cost on higher education in
Central Universities, University-wise and
category-wise as on date;
(d) whether steps would be taken to
control fee structure of professional courses
in various private and other institutions
affiliated to various universities and deemed
universities;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor?
Assistance for elementary education
in Orissa
751. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Orissa Government has

175
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
asked the Central Government for special
financial assistance for overall development
of elementary education of SCs, STs and
minority students;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which the
above proposal would be considered and
approval conveyed to the State
Government?
Central University in M.P.
†752. SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Central Universities
in the country at present, State-wise;
(b) whether Government have any
proposal under consideration for opening
a Central University in Madhya Pradesh;
and
(c) if so, by when the said proposal is
likely to be implemented?
Commission for higher education
753. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up a Commission for Higher Education;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to merge the University Grants
Commission in the new Commission;
(c) whether any draft Bill is ready on
the subject; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Funds to Madras University
754. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the funds given by the University
Grants Commission to Madras University
during 2004-05, 2005-06 and 2006-07,
respectively for new centres and new area
study programmes and grants on a one-
time basis respectively;
(b) the demands which have been
approved for 2007-08;
(c) whether it is a fact that U.G.C. has
not released such grants proportionately
to all the Universities in Andhra Pradesh;
and
(d) the details of steps likely to be taken
to allocate funds for universities in that
State for 2007-08?
Urdu units in Bihar
755. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Urdu units that were
functioning in Bihar before 1990 and how
many posts of teachers were sanctioned
then and how many of them were filled;
(b) the number of Urdu units functioning
as on date and the number of posts of Urdu
teachers lying vacant; and
(c) the measures taken to fill up the
vacant posts?
Funding pattern of Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan
756. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether some State Governments

176
have protested against the present funding
pattern of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that nearly 30
per cent of this year's Budget outlay for
SSA would remain unutilized;
(d) if so, the new funding pattern
suggested by the State Governments; and
(e) the reaction of Government in this
respect?
Establishment of national
universities
757. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
announced plans to establish 20 national
universities all over the country, to have
excellence in higher education;
(b) if so, at which locations such
universities would be set up;
(c) the criteria adopted to select places
for setting up those universities;
(d) the steps likely to be taken to
establish those universities in less
developed areas and regions; and
(e) the steps proposed to spread higher
education there?
Development of Kochin University
758. SHRI THENNALA G. BALA-
KRISHNA PILLAI: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
develop Kochin University of Science and
Technology;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the State Government has
submitted any proposal in this regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Assessment of universities and
colleges
759. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether, after National
Accreditation and Assessment Council's
survey report that 90 per cent of colleges
and 68 per cent of universities were of a
medium to poor quality, the Prime Minister
directed for making the assessment of
colleges and universities mandatory and
asked the Ministry to work out the
modalities with the aim to increase
enrolment in higher education from the
current 10 per cent to 15 per cent by
2011-12;
(b) whether UGC has also decided to
increase infrastructure in the existing
institutes, to enhance capacity and open
new universities and colleges; and
(c) if so, the details of the steps taken
so far?
Bill for foreign education providers
760. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are proposing
a Bill to open up the country's education
sector to foreign education providers;
(b) if so, whether Government had any
consultations with stakeholders in the

177
country's educational system such as
students' organizations, organizations
representing the teaching community, etc.;
(c) if so, the outcome of such
consultations; and
(d) if not, whether Government would
consider to undertake the consultation
process?
Vocationalisation of secondary
education
761. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL:
SHRI KESHUBHAI S.
PATEL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether vocationalisation of
secondary education is a centrally
sponsored scheme;
(b) whether the scheme is also
being implemented by the Gujarat
Government;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
have not released the amount of Rs. 4.67
crore, as part of the grant under the scheme;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(e) by when the remaining part of the
grant would be made available to the State
Government?
Anti-ragging committees
762. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain Central
Universities have not constituted anti-
ragging committees as required under
Supreme Court's directions;
(b) if so, the names of these universities
and the reasons for their not following
Supreme Court's directions; and
(c) the action taken by Government in
the matter and by when the concerned
universities are likely to constitute anti-
ragging committee?
Vacancies in Kendriya Vidyalayas in
North Eastern Region
763. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 5,000 posts
of teachers are lying vacant in the Kendriya
Vidyalayas of North Eastern Region;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether the local talent available in
abundance is being taped to control the
situation?
Stoppage of ragging
764. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are taking any
step to stop ragging in colleges as the new
academic year is about to start; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Drop out in Jharkhand
765. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the drop out rate in
Jharkhand is above 80 per cent;
(b) the literacy rate amoung the tribals
of the State during the last three years;
gender-wise;
(c) the school drop out among the
tribals of the state ; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
retain tribal children in schools and improve
the tribal human resource?

178
Adult Education and Literacy Mission
766. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Knowledge
Commission has, in a recent draft paper,
suggested that the responsibility of adult
education programmes should continue to
be vested with the Central Government to
prevent further deportation of the
programme and also stressed the need to
reinvent the national literacy mission so
that it should be more vibrant and relevant
to its target population;
(b) the details about the other
suggestions made through the draft paper;
(c) the number of suggestions
considered by Government; and
(d) the steps taken to implement them?
FDI in higher education
767. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Group of Ministers,
set up to give recommendations on Foreign
Direct Investment in higher education has
recommended 50 per cent FDI in higher
education and has suggested that only well-
recognized and established universities both
from the country and abroad should be
allowed to set-up campuses in the country;
and
(b) if so, by when a final decision for
introducing amendments to be incorporated
in the University Grants Commission Act
in this regard would be taken?
Stopping of ragging
768. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have been unable to stop ragging completely
in all the colleges and institutions;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether inspite of Government's
recent action to stop ragging, incidents like
eve-teasing are increasing in colleges; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Kendriya Vidyalayas in Gulbarga
769. SHRI K.B. SHANAPPA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up two Kendriya Vidyalayas in Gulbarga
in Karnataka;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) if not, the details of criteria adopted
for setting up a Kendriya Vidyalaya in a
district?
Compulsory education of children
†770. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made
fresh estimate of expenditure to be incurred
on the programme for providing
compulsory education to the children
between the age group of 6 to 13 years in
the country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

179
(b) if so, the details thereof and to what
extent it is higher or lower than the prior
estimate;
(c) whether sources for obtaining the
required amount have been identified; and
